q: Which built-in role lets a user view everything in a subscription but change nothing?
exp: Reader can view all resources but cannot make changes.

q: Which types of security principal can receive an Azure role assignment?
opts: Users, groups, service principals, and managed identities
exp: Role assignments target users, groups, service principals, or managed identities. Devices cannot be assigned roles.

q: What is the smallest scope at which you can assign an Azure role?
exp: Roles can be assigned at management group, subscription, resource group, or individual resource scope.

q: A developer must manage virtual machines in RG-Dev but must NOT be able to manage the virtual network or the storage accounts. Least-privilege role?
exp: Virtual Machine Contributor manages VMs but not the VNet or storage accounts they connect to.

q: An engineer needs to manage VNets, NSGs, and load balancers in a subscription without access to VMs. Which role?
exp: Network Contributor manages networking resources only.

q: An app needs to read blobs in a storage account using Microsoft Entra authentication. Which role assignment is least privileged?
opts: Storage Blob Data Reader on the container or account
exp: Blob data access needs a data-plane role such as Storage Blob Data Reader. Reader and Storage Account Contributor are control-plane roles.

q: A finance user must view invoices and billing data but not resources. Which role?
exp: Billing Reader grants read access to billing data only.

q: A user must view cost data and create budgets but not modify resources. Which role fits best?
exp: Cost Management Contributor can view costs and manage cost configuration such as budgets and exports.

q: In the portal, where do you add a role assignment for a resource group?
opts: Resource group → Access control (IAM) → Add role assignment
exp: Access control (IAM) is the RBAC blade on every scope.

q: You want to find out what roles a specific user has on a resource group, including inherited ones. Fastest portal tool?
exp: Check access shows a principal's assignments and inherited access at that scope.

q: Which CLI command lists all role assignments for a user, including those inherited from higher scopes?
exp: az role assignment list with --assignee, --all and --include-inherited returns assignments across scopes including inherited ones.

q: Which PowerShell cmdlet assigns a role?
exp: New-AzRoleAssignment creates a role assignment; New-AzRoleDefinition creates a custom role.

q: A subscription reaches its role assignment limit. What's the recommended way to reduce assignments?
opts: Assign roles to groups instead of individual users
exp: Each subscription has a role assignment limit (4,000). Assigning roles to groups uses fewer assignments.

q: User1 is Owner of RG1. An administrator applies a ReadOnly lock to RG1. Can User1 delete a VM in RG1?
opts: No — locks apply to all users regardless of role
exp: Locks override RBAC permissions for everyone. The lock must be removed first (Owner can remove it).

q: Azure RBAC is built on which service?
exp: Azure RBAC is an authorization system built on Azure Resource Manager.

q: User1 has Contributor on Sub1. Which TWO actions can User1 NOT perform?
opts: Create a VM in any resource group of Sub1
Assign the Reader role to User2 on Sub1
Delete a resource group in Sub1
Create a resource lock on a resource group
exp: Contributor cannot write to Microsoft.Authorization, which covers role assignments and locks.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: A role can be assigned to a managed identity
Role assignments to a group apply to its members
A Reader at the subscription scope can read resources in every resource group of that subscription
Removing a user from Entra ID automatically deletes their role assignments
exp: Managed identities and groups can hold roles; Reader inherits down; deleting a user leaves orphaned 'Identity not found' assignments that should be cleaned up.

q: After moving a subscription to a different Entra tenant, users from the old tenant can no longer manage resources. Why?
opts: All role assignments are permanently removed when a subscription changes tenant
The subscription is disabled for 30 days
exp: Changing the directory removes all Azure RBAC role assignments; you must recreate them in the new tenant.

q: What do Azure RBAC 'conditions' (ABAC) allow you to do on top of role assignments?
opts: Add attribute-based checks, for example limiting blob access by blob index tags
Deny all access to a tenant
exp: Role assignment conditions add fine-grained ABAC checks, for example on storage blob attributes.

q: Admins must activate the Owner role only when needed, for a limited time, with approval. Which feature?
opts: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (eligible assignments)
exp: PIM provides eligible, time-bound, approval-based role activation. It requires P2/Governance licensing.

q: Which built-in role allows managing resource locks and role assignments but not other resources?
exp: User Access Administrator has Microsoft.Authorization/* rights, which cover assignments and locks.

q: A role is assigned at the Tenant Root Group management group. What does it cover?
opts: All management groups, subscriptions, and resources in the tenant
Nothing; assignments at root aren't allowed
exp: The tenant root group is the top of the hierarchy, so assignments there inherit to everything below.

q: Which statement best describes the Owner role?
opts: Full access to manage all resources, including assigning roles in Azure RBAC
exp: Owner = Contributor rights + role assignment rights.

q: A user is in Group A (Reader on RG1) and Group B (Contributor on RG1). There is no deny assignment. Effective permission on RG1?
exp: RBAC is additive. The union of Reader and Contributor gives Contributor capabilities.

q: What happens when a deny assignment conflicts with a role assignment that allows the same action?
opts: The deny assignment wins — deny takes precedence
exp: Deny assignments block actions even if a role assignment grants them.

q: Which section of a custom role controls data-plane operations such as reading blob contents?
exp: DataActions and NotDataActions define data-plane operations; Actions covers the control plane.

q: What is the quickest way to create a custom role similar to an existing built-in role in the portal?
opts: IAM → Roles → select a built-in role → Clone
exp: The portal lets you clone a role and then edit its permissions.

q: Which CLI command creates a custom role from a JSON file?
exp: az role definition create accepts a JSON role definition.

q: Can a custom role use the root scope "/" in AssignableScopes?
opts: No — custom roles can't use root scope; only built-in roles are available there
exp: Custom roles can list management groups, subscriptions, and resource groups, but not the root scope "/".

q: How many management groups can a custom role list in AssignableScopes?
exp: A custom role can include only one management group in AssignableScopes.

q: A custom role has Actions ["Microsoft.Compute/*"] and NotActions ["Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/delete"]. The user also has Contributor on the same scope. Can they delete a VM?
opts: Yes — NotActions doesn't block permissions granted by another role
No — custom roles override built-in roles
Only if the VM is stopped
exp: NotActions just removes permissions from that one role's grant. Contributor still grants delete.

q: What does the wildcard in "Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/*" grant?
opts: All operations on storage accounts and their child control-plane resources
exp: The wildcard grants every control-plane operation under that resource type path. Data access requires DataActions.

q: Which operation string allows a user to start virtual machines?
exp: VM operations follow the Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/<operation>/action format.

q: Order the steps to create and use a custom role via CLI:
items: Assign the role with az role assignment create
Write the role definition JSON (Actions, AssignableScopes)
Verify it with az role definition list --custom-role-only
exp: Write the JSON → create the definition → verify it exists → assign it.

q: Answer Yes or No about custom roles:
stmts: Custom roles can be shared across subscriptions that trust the same tenant
A custom role can be assigned outside its AssignableScopes
Custom roles require Entra ID P1 or P2
exp: Custom roles are usable within listed scopes in the same tenant; they cannot be assigned outside AssignableScopes; no Entra premium license is needed; DataActions are supported.

q: Which role should a monitoring team get to view metrics and logs and create alert rules, without changing resources?
exp: Monitoring Contributor can read monitoring data and edit monitoring settings, such as alerts and diagnostic settings.

q: A user must only read monitoring data such as metrics and logs. Which role?
exp: Monitoring Reader can read all monitoring data.

q: A backup operator must manage backups (start backup, restore) but not delete backup data or vaults. Which role?
exp: Backup Operator can run backups and restores but cannot remove backup data, create vaults or grant access. Backup Contributor can also manage backup policies and remove backup data.

q: Which role lets a user connect to a VM via Microsoft Entra login with administrator privileges inside the OS?
exp: Entra-based VM login uses Virtual Machine Administrator Login (admin rights in the OS) or Virtual Machine User Login (standard user). VM Contributor doesn't grant OS login.

q: You assign the Reader role to a guest user on RG1. What does the guest see in the Azure portal?
opts: The resources in RG1, after switching to your directory
exp: Guests switch directories in the portal and see only resources where they have role assignments.

ctx: Assignments: User1 — Owner on RG-A. User2 — User Access Administrator on Sub1 (contains RG-A). User3 — Contributor on Sub1.
q: Which users can grant User4 the Reader role on RG-A?
exp: Owner and User Access Administrator can write role assignments; UAA at Sub1 inherits to RG-A. Contributor cannot.

ctx: User1 has Reader on management group MG1 (contains Sub1) and Virtual Machine Contributor on RG-VMs in Sub1.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: User1 can restart a VM in RG-VMs
User1 can create a virtual network in RG-VMs
User1 can view storage accounts in other resource groups of Sub1
User1 can assign Reader to another user on RG-VMs
exp: VM Contributor covers VM restart but not creating VNets; Reader inherited from MG1 covers all of Sub1; neither role writes role assignments.

q: Where are Microsoft Entra directory roles (like User Administrator) assigned?
exp: Directory roles are managed in Entra ID's Roles and administrators blade, not in Azure IAM.

q: Which Entra role is the most privileged and should be assigned to as few people as possible?
exp: Global Administrator has full access to all directory features. Microsoft recommends fewer than five.

q: Can a group be assigned a Microsoft Entra directory role?
opts: Yes, if the group was created as role-assignable (isAssignableToRole = true)
exp: Only role-assignable groups (a flag set at creation, which can't be dynamic) can receive Entra roles.

q: A user needs to manage app registrations and enterprise applications only. Least-privilege Entra role?
exp: Application Administrator manages app registrations and enterprise apps.

q: A VM-hosted app must access Key Vault without storing credentials in code. What should you use?
opts: A managed identity for the VM, granted access to Key Vault
A user's password in app settings
exp: Managed identities provide Azure-managed credentials for Entra authentication; you grant the identity RBAC roles on the target.

q: Five VMs need the SAME identity with the same permissions, and the identity must survive if a VM is deleted. Which type?
exp: User-assigned identities are standalone resources, can be shared across resources, and have an independent lifecycle. System-assigned identities are deleted with their resource.

q: What happens to a system-assigned managed identity when its VM is deleted?
exp: System-assigned identities are tied to the resource lifecycle and are removed with it.

q: Order the steps so a web app can read secrets from Key Vault (RBAC permission model) without credentials:
items: Assign 'Key Vault Secrets User' to the identity on the vault
Enable a system-assigned managed identity on the web app
Reference the secret from the app using its identity
Confirm the vault uses the Azure RBAC permission model
exp: Enable the identity → confirm the vault uses RBAC → assign the data role → the app reads secrets with its identity.
